newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals end shortened session firmer.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals end shortened session firmer.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based precious metal futures ended firmer in Friday's abbreviated half-day session, lifted by modest gains in bullion prices overnight and expectations of a further weakening of the yen, traders said.
They added that trade was light due to the year-end holidays, however.
The London bullion markets were closed overnight for Boxing Day and TOCOM will be closed all of next week for the New Year's holidays. TOCOM will reopen on January 6.
TOCOM benchmark December 1997 gold ended five yen higher at 1,354 yen per gram. The other months were up five to seven yen.

Individual investors were light net sellers of TOCOM gold as longs liquidated positions, traders said, but expectations of further dips in the yen against the dollar helped keep sellers at bay. The yen fell Thursday to a fresh 44-month low of more than 115 to the dollar.
Gold bullion was quoted at $369.05/35 an ounce at 0235 GMT, virtually unchanged from New York's closing quote of $369.00/50 and up slightly from Tokyo's Thursday close at $368.30/80.
One bullion dealer expected bullion to hold firm and perhaps test resistance at $372 in the near term, supported by prospects for short-covering from overseas investors.
TOCOM platinum was flat to firmer, as some individual investors rolled long positions forward, traders said.
Benchmark December 1997 platinum settled five better at 1,366 yen per gram, while the remaining months were flat to seven higher.
TOCOM December palladium ended two higher at 434 yen per gram, while December silver was up 0.6 yen at 180.6 yen per 10 grams.
